svg.title: Fourth, tritone, fifth
svg.desc: Fourth, tritone, fifth. A keyboard from C4 to C5 with C4 as the shared root and the upper notes F4 (P4, 5 semitones), F♯4 = G♭4 (A4/d5, 6 semitones), G4 (P5, 7 semitones) each in its own identity colour. A table lists what stayed (root C4) and what changed (upper note, semitone count, and the Plogger shape, shadow and fill where they apply).

g.text: C4 to F4 (5), F♯4/G♭4 (6) and G4 (7): three neighbouring keys.
P4 → A4: +1 semitone on the upper note · A4 → P5: +1 semitone on the upper note
The tritone is 6 semitones. Written F♯ above C it is an augmented fourth (A4); written G♭
it is a diminished fifth (d5). Same key, two correct names.
HOW TO READ THE THREE PLOGGER MARKS
A Shape (outline): jagged = dissonant family · rounded = modal family · straight = perfect-group
family. A family label, not a measured sound wave.
B Shadow (side): ← Fundamental [1]–[5] · ↔ Both [6] · → Octave [7]–[11]. Always paired with its
C Fill (inside): dense/dark = non-harmonic · open/light = harmonic · midtone dotted = neutral [6]
A historic teaching lens (Archived printed pictograph (R2_pictograph_reference.html) and
app/DiChordPictograph.tsx), not acoustic law. The identity colour is a separate, artistic label.
